result.summary: Adds an optional `precious` parameter to the Mining IPC `submitBlock` and `BlockTemplate.submitSolution` methods so external miners can submit and prioritize a block against competing equal-work tips in a single call. To support this atomically, `PreciousBlock` in validation is updated to execute under `m_chainstate_mutex` without releasing the lock and reports whether the block was successfully connected to the active chain. The change also introduces new Cap'n Proto interface ordinals and deprecates the prior method signatures with explicit error responses.
result.problem: External mining clients communicating over IPC cannot prioritize a mined block over a same-work competing block in one operation; they must make a subsequent `preciousblock` RPC call. This multi-call sequence requires extra round-trips and introduces race conditions with concurrent chain activations.
evidence: PR description: 'With this change, IPC mining clients can submit and prefer a block in one IPC call, instead of submitting it over IPC and then using the preciousblock RPC separately.'

Commit 64e5010615: 'Hold m_chainstate_mutex while marking a block precious, activating the best chain, and capturing whether the block is in the active chain... Return this status through the connected output so mining submissions can inspect the result without racing another chain activation.'
result.scope_notes: Touches Cap'n Proto IPC interface definitions, introducing new method IDs and stubbing deprecated ones with exceptions. Includes a test refactoring moving proof-of-work grinding loops across multiple test suites into a shared `GrindBlock` helper.
result.changed_since_previous: No substantial functional or architectural changes; the scope and implementation remain consistent with the earlier version.
result.card: This pull request adds an optional precious argument to the IPC Mining submitBlock and submitSolution interfaces. External mining software can now submit a block and prioritize it against equal-work tips in a single call instead of issuing a subsequent preciousblock RPC. To prevent activation race conditions, validation's PreciousBlock now holds the chainstate mutex throughout reorg evaluation and reports whether the block connected. The PR also deprecates older Cap'n Proto interface ordinals with explicit client update errors and deduplicates test proof-of-work grinding.

risk.why: Modifies locking and execution flow in chainstate activation and PreciousBlock, which could cause deadlocks or improper chain tip selection if locking guarantees fail.
